findings.summary: The edge-case page relies on LEFT JOIN anti-joins, GROUP BY/HAVING, COUNT and self joins before any of them is taught.
findings.evidence: "LEFT JOIN employees e ON e.dept_id = d.id WHERE e.id IS NULL", "GROUP BY email HAVING COUNT(*) > 1", and "A self join loses the CEO row" all appear on page 3, while joins, aggregates and HAVING are first taught on pages 7-10.
findings.fix: Show only IS NULL and plain SELECT on this page, with the edge cases listed in prose. Move the anti-join, duplicate-email and self-join demonstrations to the pages that teach those tools, or label this page a preview and point to those pages.

findings.summary: Q37, the JOIN USING example, is built on a WITH CTE and GROUP BY 1 before CTEs are taught.

findings.summary: The text says a FROM subquery must have an alias, but PostgreSQL 16, the engine this handbook targets, made the alias optional.
findings.evidence: "a FROM subquery needs an alias"; "A `FROM` subquery must have an ==alias=="; table row "FROM (aliased)"
findings.fix: Say the alias is optional from PostgreSQL 16 and still required on 15 and earlier. Keep the alias in the examples for portability and say that is why.

findings.summary: The note says LIMIT without ORDER BY is random. It is actually unspecified: the order depends on the plan and physical layout and is not guaranteed.

findings.fix: Say "LIMIT without ORDER BY returns an arbitrary, unguaranteed set of rows".
